title: Revelation Begins With Jesus, Not the Antichrist
paragraphs:
Revelation Begins With Jesus, Not the Antichrist
The Most Misunderstood Book in the Bible Was Never Meant to Make You Fear the Future—It Was Written to Make You Fall in Love With Christ
Most people open Revelation looking for the Antichrist.
God opens Revelation by showing us Jesus.
That single mistake has caused millions of believers to read the final book of Scripture through fear instead of worship.
Meanwhile, the One standing at the center of the entire book waits to be seen.
The tragedy is that many Christians can spend years studying Revelation and still miss the very Person Revelation was written to reveal.
The book does not begin with the Antichrist.
It does not begin with the Beast.
It does not begin with the Mark.
It does not begin with judgment.
It does not begin with Armageddon.
The very first words of Revelation are impossible to ignore:
The word Apokalypsis does not mean catastrophe.
It does not mean apocalypse in the modern Hollywood sense.
It means unveiling, disclosure, revealing, uncovering something previously hidden.
The final book of Scripture is literally called:
Not the unveiling of the Antichrist.
Not the unveiling of the Beast.
Not the unveiling of global chaos.
Because if Revelation is primarily about Jesus, then every chapter must be read through Him.
For many believers, Revelation became a source of anxiety because someone taught them to start with the wrong character.
Imagine watching a movie and focusing only on the villain while ignoring the hero.
Imagine reading a love story while obsessing over the antagonist.
Imagine standing before a masterpiece while staring only at the frame.
That is what happens when Revelation becomes more about the Antichrist than Christ.
Because fear-filled Christians rarely become effective witnesses.
But believers captivated by Jesus become impossible to silence.
When the Apostle John received this revelation, he was not sitting in comfort.
Yet in the middle of suffering, heaven did not show him the power of Rome.
Then suddenly he hears a voice.
The voice of the risen Christ.
When John turns, he sees something that changes him forever.
His voice is like many waters.
His face shines like the sun.
His holiness overwhelms the human soul.
The same disciple who once leaned against Jesus at the Last Supper now collapses at His feet.
This is not because Jesus became less loving.
It is because John now sees what was hidden behind the veil of flesh.
The carpenter from Nazareth is also the King of Kings.
The Lamb is also the Lion.
The Savior is also the Judge.
The One crucified is also glorified.
And then comes one of the most beautiful moments in all Scripture.
Jesus places His hand on John.
The glorified Christ touches a trembling man.
The same Jesus whose glory causes men to collapse is the same Jesus who comforts the broken.
This is the heartbeat of Revelation.
The world often tries to separate these truths.
The Hebrew Scriptures anticipated this moment centuries earlier.
Isaiah saw a glimpse of God's glory and cried:
"Woe is me, for I am ruined." (Isaiah 6:5)
Whenever sinful humanity encounters divine holiness, the response is the same.
Yet every genuine encounter with God's holiness is followed by grace.
This pattern runs through the entire Bible.
That is why Revelation should not terrify believers.
The central message is not that darkness becomes stronger.
The central message is that Jesus remains sovereign.
Nothing in Revelation suggests that evil is winning.
In fact, the opposite is true.
Every chapter moves history toward the complete victory of Jesus Christ.
The Father never abandons His plan.
The Holy Spirit never stops working.
The Church never stops belonging to Christ.
The cross never loses its power.
And grace never stops reaching sinners.
Perhaps that is why so many people avoid Revelation.
Revelation reminds us that Jesus is not merely a life coach.
The Greek word repeatedly used is:
And every human heart must answer the same question.
But Revelation relentlessly pulls our eyes back to the throne.
Because whoever occupies the throne of your heart determines the direction of your life.
Maybe that is why this message feels personal.
Because deep down, every one of us knows what it feels like to chase lesser kings.
We know what it feels like to build identities around things that eventually fail us.
We know what it feels like to search for meaning in places that leave us empty.
We know what it feels like to smile publicly while quietly carrying fear.
But Revelation points us toward the One who cannot fail.
"I am the Alpha and the Omega."

Ἐγώ εἰμι τὸ Ἄλφα καὶ τὸ Ὦ
(Egō eimi to Alpha kai to Ō)
The author and finisher of history.
The One who writes the first sentence and the final chapter.
And if He holds history in His hands, He can hold your life too.
The greatest scandal in human history was not political corruption.
It was humanity's rebellion against God.
The greatest grace in human history was not self-improvement.
It was Jesus stepping into that rebellion and carrying our punishment to the cross.
The same Christ revealed in Revelation is the same Christ crucified at Calvary.
Because Revelation was never written merely to satisfy curiosity about the future.
It was written to create devotion to Jesus in the present.
And perhaps today, that is exactly what your heart needs.
The One who still says, "Fear not."
The One who still rewrites broken stories.
The One who still turns scandal into grace.
If this article helped you see Jesus more clearly, don't keep it to yourself.
What part of Revelation has impacted your walk with Jesus the most?
Your testimony may encourage someone else today.
Every article, devotional, teaching resource, and discipleship tool exists to point people toward Jesus Christ and the transforming power of the Gospel.
Most importantly, your support helps expand Gospel-centered outreach and allows more people to encounter the life-changing message of Jesus Christ.
One day every headline will be forgotten, every empire will be dust, every prophecy fulfilled, and every eye fixed on the One Revelation was revealing all along.
